name: Self-Improvement Metacognition Loop
summary: After every task: reflect on what worked, what failed, what was improvised. Update skills to capture improvements.

steps.note: Ask internally: (1) Did I improvise any steps? (2) Did I retry anything? (3) Did I encounter unexpected errors? (4) Was the output exactly what was requested?

steps.action: IF YES to any → call write_skill immediately
steps.note: Capture: what went wrong, what fix worked, what to do differently next time. Include AVOID: notes for anti-patterns.

steps.action: IF skill already exists → increment version
steps.note: write_skill auto-increments version. Version >= 2 = battle-tested. Version >= 5 = mastered.
Scan for: (a) thin skills with < 3 steps, (b) skills not used recently, (c) skills that contradicted each other. Upgrade or delete.
During dream cycles: read all skills, identify gaps, write 1-2 new or improved skills based on session patterns.

notes: The goal is compounding improvement: every session you should know slightly more than the last
A failed task with a write_skill call is better than a successful task with no reflection
Skills are your long-term memory. Without them, you reset every session.
Quality signal: if you had to guess at a step, the skill for that domain is missing or incomplete
